title: Colour and state
description: How a cell gets its colour: the twenty-one Slurm states and the nine colours they resolve to, the same states drawn live, the three continuous modes that colour by occupancy instead of by state, and the shape channel.

panels.title: The states, and the colour each one gets

options.content: Nine colours for twenty-one states. The hue says what an operator does about the node; the shade inside a hue says the degree, never the decision. The exact state is always spelled out in the tooltip and in the accessible label, in every colour mode. | | Theme name | What it decides | States it covers | |---|---|---|---| | `#96D98D` | `light-green` | **it works** | `allocated, allocated+, allocated-` | | `#73BF69` | `green` | **it works** | `mixed, mix, mixed-` | | `#56A64B` | `semi-dark-green` | **it works** | `completing, comp` | | `#5794F2` | `blue` | **capacity sitting free** | `idle, idle-` | | `#8AB8FF` | `light-blue` | **capacity sitting free** | `planned, plnd` | | `#8F3BB8` | `dark-purple` | **a human claimed it** | `drained, draining, drng, maintenance, reserved, resv, npc, perfctrs` | | `#FF9830` | `orange` | **not answering, or moving** | `the * suffix, blocked, reboot` | | `#C4162A` | `dark-red` | **broken** | `down, fail, unknown, invalid` | | the theme's own ink | `text` | **absent from the floor** | `the ~ suffix, power_down, powering_up, future` | Hex values are the dark theme's. Every colour is a Grafana theme name rather than a literal, so a light theme or a custom one resolves its own value and the panel follows the dashboard around it. Protanopia and deuteranopia collapse the red-green axis and keep light against dark, which is why what works is drawn light and what is broken is drawn dark: `green` against `red` measures ΔE 32 to a full-colour reader and **4.6** to a deuteranope, while `light-green` against `dark-red` is 32 and **25**.

panels.description: The nine colours and the six decisions they carry, as documented. Hand-written, so read it beside the panel to its right, which renders the same rules and cannot drift.

panels.title: Every mapping, resolved live
panels.description: The table beside this one is written by hand and nothing checks it; this is the same rules rendered by the panel, so it cannot drift from what ships. It is also a longer list on purpose: the table groups twenty-one states into nine colours, while sinfo writes each of them several ways - alloc and allocated, drng and draining, plus the suffix forms - and every spelling has to resolve. The last one, a_state_slurm_adds_tomorrow, is not a Slurm state and never will be. It stands in for whatever a future Slurm introduces: drawn as a hollow ring rather than coloured by accident, named in the strip above, and printed with the exact rule to paste under Value mappings - delimited, so Grafana does not wrap it into an exact match.

panels.title: CPU utilisation by node
panels.description: slurm_node_cpu_alloc over slurm_node_cpu_total. Pale is empty, dark is full. Hover for the exact figures.

panels.title: Memory utilisation by node
panels.description: slurm_node_mem_alloc over slurm_node_mem_total. A node pale here and dark on CPU is the classic memory-starved job shape.

panels.title: GPU utilisation by node
panels.description: Only the partitions that have GPUs: eight per node on gpu, two on visu. Filtering is done in the query rather than left to the panel, because a grid of 540 cells where 440 are empty outlines is four fifths of nothing - the empty cell is right, it just should not be the whole panel. A node with no GPU is still drawn empty rather than zero wherever one turns up; NodeCell's own tests pin that.

panels.title: Shape channel off, the default
panels.description: The floor as it ships. Colour alone carries the state, which is safe for a full-colour reader: the palette beside this is measured, and its worst pair in normal vision is well clear of the floor. Compare it with the panel to its right - same nodes, same colours, one option apart.

panels.title: Shape channel on
panels.description: The same floor with Display > Shape channel switched on. A notch or a diagonal cut marks the states whose fill is not safe on its own: "not responding" against "allocated" is Delta E 4.8 under protanopia, below any legal floor, and no arrangement of the six theme hues cleared it. The shape is not a second alphabet for all twenty-one states - it marks two families, and every other state stays a plain square. Off by default because the notches cost legibility at fourteen pixels for every reader who does not need them; one click away for those who do.
